articles.title: Sinkhole opens in Vaughan after Wednesday’s storm, forcing indefinite closure on Huntington Road
articles.summary: A stretch of roadway in Vaughan has been shut down indefinitely after a sinkhole opened during Wednesday’s intense storm system — a fast‑moving, flood‑triggering blast of rain that hammered the GTA and much of southern Ontario. articles.title: Gloria Steinem, a potent voice of US feminism and co-founder of Ms. Magazine, dies at 92
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Gloria Steinem, the celebrated author and activist who became one of the most visible symbols and potent voices of the U.S. women’s movement and a fierce advocate for feminist causes for over six decades, has died. She was 92.

articles.title: Complaints about drug use, violence persist at Barbara Hall Park as Toronto considers its response
articles.summary: A Toronto city task force meant to address ongoing issues at Barbara Hall Park is expected to revisit its approach amid ongoing complaints about public drug use and violence in the area.

articles.title: 74-year-old man charged for child abduction in Caledon: police
articles.summary: A 74-year-old man has been charged after an attempted abduction of a child last Saturday evening in Caledon, Ontario Provincial Police say.

articles.title: Pickering teen hospitalized with life-altering injuries after e-scooter crash
articles.summary: A 16-year-old boy is in hospital with life-altering injuries after his electric scooter collided with a vehicle in Pickering Tuesday night.

articles.title: Carney's 'hydronym' moment is behind a cheeky campaign to raise awareness about Lake Ontario
articles.summary: Riding on Prime Minister Mark Carney's use of the proper word for a body of water, a London, Ont., company has created T-shirts emblazoned with "My hydronyms are Lake and Ontario." A portion of the apparel sales proceeds go to Swim Drink Fish Canada, a charity that connects people with the lake, and works to keep it safe and clean.
